name: Total Football (Totaalvoetbal)
scopeNote: Idea, not one team: Dutch 'totaalvoetbal' as practised by Michels' Ajax (1965-71, European Cup 1971), Kovacs' Ajax (1971-73, two more European Cups) and Michels' Netherlands (1974 World Cup, final 7 July 1974). Start 1965-01-01 is approximate ('By January 1965', These Football Times). Core as sources describe it: positional interchange within a kept structure, space control (big in possession, small out of it), high pressing and an offside-trap high line, fit versatile players. Popular label 'position-swapping' alone understates pressing/space, which Michels and Neeskens stress. Exemplar ids: manager rinus-michels, team ajax-1971-73, team netherlands-1974. Contributors not catalog ids: Johan Cruyff (on-pitch conductor, roaming centre forward, later Barcelona) and Stefan/Istvan Kovacs (Ajax coach 1971-73, popularised the term in 1972). Precursors (influences): Jack Reynolds, Vic Buckingham, Hugo Meisl's Wunderteam, Sebes' Hungary, Brazil 4-2-4. Marking of Ajax's own defence (zonal vs man) not evidenced by any verified source; only the opposition man-marking of Vogts on Cruyff in 1974. No verified set-piece or Coaches' Voice material found.
openQuestions: Origin of the name: Auke Kok (via Neerlandistiek) says Michels used 'totaalvoetbal' in a Limburgsch Dagblad interview on 12 Sept 1965; Van den Nieuwenhof says Michels used it only occasionally in 1965 and it became known in 1972 when Kovacs described the club's style so; Winner says it entered Dutch in 1974 with the World Cup; Kok (2004) credits journalist Maarten de Vos. Primary 1965 interview not seen.

Michels reportedly disliked the term and preferred a pressing description (single coaching-interview claim in a search summary, not verified); These Football Times itself suggests 'Proactive Football'. Label supported by evidence: 'totaalvoetbal' / Hollandse school, with pressing and space as core, not only interchange.

Exemplars differ: Michels' Ajax (1965-71) used a 4-2-4-derived oscillating shape with Vasovic as libero (SI); Kovacs' Ajax kept the approach (Guide to Football, Spielverlagerung) but his own tactical view was not found; Netherlands 1974 had Michels arriving on the eve of the tournament, and Neeskens says the pressing blueprint 'hadn't clicked yet' before the tournament; Rijsbergen says the goalkeeper acted as libero outside the area.

Invention credit contested: SI says Michels 'did not pioneer' it; Spielverlagerung credits Reynolds; Wikipedia lists Meisl/Hogan/Sebes. Michels is credited with the paradigm of space and with fitness-based pressing.
Michels quote 'war' varies: 'Football is something like war' (TFT) vs 'Professional football is something like war' (blog); date unknown.
Mid-1960s start: sources disagree on Michels' appointment date (Wikipedia-derived pages vs 'By January 1965'); confirm day.
Zonal vs man marking in Ajax/Netherlands defence not established; need Coaches' Voice, Cox 'Zonal Marking' or Winner text.
statedView dates for quotes 0, 2, 4, 5 are the publication date of the page quoting them; the original date of utterance was not found.

statedView.quote: If you have the ball you must make the field as big as possible, and if you don't have the ball you must make it as small as possible.

There has been only one real tactical revolution and it happened when football shifted from an individual to a collective game. It happened with Ajax first and then the Holland national team at the beginning of the 1970s.
